fact: RAG combines pre-trained parametric memory (the transformer neural network weights) with non-parametric memory (an external dense vector index of text passages).
source_name: Lewis et al. (2020) - Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks (NeurIPS 2020)

fact: In standard RAG inference, the external knowledge can be updated, expanded, or replaced without modifying, retraining, or fine-tuning the underlying model weights.
RAG significantly reduces factual hallucinations on knowledge-intensive tasks compared to pure parametric generation by grounding answers in retrieved source text.
Dense Passage Retrieval (DPR) uses neural bi-encoders to convert text queries and document passages into continuous dense vector representations for similarity search.
source_name: Karpukhin et al. (2020) / Lewis et al. (2020) Section 2.1

fact: Lewis et al. formulated two RAG variants: RAG-Sequence (uses the same retrieved passages for the entire generated response) and RAG-Token (can select different passages for each generated token).
Document chunking breaks large source files into smaller semantic pieces so passages fit within the LLM context window and preserve retrieval precision.
Embeddings are dense numerical vectors representing the semantic meaning of text chunks, allowing distance metrics like cosine similarity to find topical matches.
source_name: Google Cloud Generative AI - Text Embeddings Guide

fact: A vector database indexes high-dimensional embeddings to perform fast approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search across millions of text chunks.
source_name: Pinecone Learning Center - What is a Vector Database?

fact: In prompt augmentation, the most relevant retrieved passages are appended directly into the prompt along with the user's question before generation.
source_name: Hugging Face Transformers Documentation - RAG Models

fact: RAG has limitations: if retrieval fails to find the correct document chunk, the generator cannot provide the right answer (retrieval bottleneck), and retrieval introduces latency.
source_name: Lewis et al. (2020) Section 5 & AWS Architecture Center

fact: RAG provides direct source provenance and citations because the model references the explicit external documents used during generation.
Decoupling static language generation from external knowledge stores makes RAG substantially cheaper and more agile than continuous full-model retraining.
source_name: Meta AI Engineering Blog - Retrieval-Augmented Generation
